text: I do not claim that this measure is equivalent to a dictatorship.
rationale: negated comparison: keeps "dictatorship" but denies the equivalence.

text: Raising the retirement age is nothing like a thief taking money.
rationale: negated comparison: keeps "thief" but denies it.

text: He was called a 'thief', but the accusation is not supported by the evidence presented.
rationale: quoted and contested: the charged word is reported, not asserted.

text: Critics labelled the plan 'authoritarian', a characterisation the report disputes.
rationale: quoted and contested: label attributed to others and disputed.

text: We can cut costs or raise revenue, and other options exist too.
rationale: open alternatives: explicitly more than two options.

text: People can support the reform, amend it, or reject it.
rationale: open alternatives: three options, no forced binary.

text: The measure may have contributed to the price rise, but the effect depends on several factors.
rationale: cautious causation: hedged, no causal assertion from sequence.

text: Crime rose after the party took power, though researchers have not established a cause.
rationale: cautious causation: sequence stated, cause explicitly left open.

text: The report was late three times this year, as the minutes confirm; the committee will discuss the delay.
rationale: verified presupposition: the premise is explicitly confirmed in context.

text: Is this council corrupt? Investigators have opened a formal inquiry to find out.
rationale: genuine question: open, with the inquiry answering it, not asserting.

text: Either we accept the proposal, or we do nothing at all.
rationale: inverse case: false dilemma with mild, non-charged words.

text: Sales dropped after the packaging changed, so the packaging reduced sales.
rationale: inverse case: implied causation with neutral vocabulary.

text: The committee will review the agency's repeated delays this quarter.
rationale: inverse case: presupposes repeated delays, no charged words.

text: When asked about our timeline, we bring up their timeline from last year.
rationale: inverse case: whataboutism with plain words.

text: Why should we keep funding a program that never works?
rationale: inverse case: loaded rhetorical question, mild vocabulary.

text: Approving this budget is the same as approving every future budget.
rationale: inverse case: manufactured equivalence without charged words.
